Holding each horizon λ,e fixed, define z=x-e, η_i=(1-e_(i+1)²)z_i−2e_i e_(i+1)z_(i+1), c_i=e_i(1-e_(i+1)²), p_(i+1)/p_i=2e_(i+1)²/(1-e_(i+1)²), normalized Σp_i=1. Strict convexity of (1−y²)^(-1/2) implies uniform nonnegative quadratic lower bound for each d_i in successor deviation, including boundary cases; compactness of the equilibrium cube gives Σp_i d_i>=κΣ z_j². Integrate over [0,T], use actual horizon means λ_i and compact storage to get average terminal output +mκ average squared deviation <=R(λ)+C/T, independent of control regularity. If Cesàro means converge, continuity yields limsup and turnpike consequence. For n=1 unit rates starting from occupancy 1, equilibrium e=(√5−1)/2 and transient integral ∫(x-e)dt=log[(e+2)/(2e+1)]>0, so 1/T is uniformly optimal order.
